FR-001.title: The player experience MUST provide no command, board entry, or other selectable action that directly forces puzzle success.

FR-002.title: The player experience MUST remove the former administrator shortcut that bulk-removes incorrect passwords.

FR-003.title: The game master MUST retain a solve control that completes an active unsolved puzzle without consuming an attempt.

FR-004.title: A game-master solve action MUST publish the solved result to every connected player through the normal shared success flow.

FR-005.title: A special pattern MUST begin and end with one matching pair from the four allowed bracket types.

FR-006.title: A special pattern MUST have its opening and closing bracket on the same horizontal board row.

FR-007.title: A special pattern MUST contain no alphabetic characters between its opening and closing bracket.

FR-008.title: Pointing to the opening bracket of an unused valid pattern MUST highlight the entire pattern through its matching closing bracket.

FR-009.title: Selecting an unused valid pattern MUST produce exactly one effect for the shared puzzle.

FR-010.title: When at least one incorrect password remains, each valid pattern activation MUST have an 80% chance to remove one incorrect password and a 20% chance to restore attempts.

FR-011.title: A dud-removal effect MUST replace exactly one selectable incorrect password with periods without removing the correct password.

FR-012.title: An attempt-restoration effect MUST return remaining attempts to the puzzle maximum without exceeding that maximum.

FR-013.title: Each newly generated board MUST contain a random number of valid special patterns from 3 through 6 inclusive.

FR-014.title: The special-pattern count range MUST NOT vary by hacking difficulty.

FR-015.title: Each distinct opening-position and closing-position pair MUST be usable at most once during a puzzle.

FR-016.title: Multiple compatible opening brackets MUST each form a separate pattern when they share a compatible closing bracket on the same row.

FR-017.title: Using one stacked pattern MUST NOT consume another pattern with a different opening position.

FR-018.title: Replacing a dud with periods MUST immediately make any newly valid pattern selectable during the same puzzle.

FR-019.title: When no incorrect password remains, an otherwise valid dud-removal outcome MUST restore attempts instead.

FR-020.title: Pattern activation, pattern availability, used-pattern state, removed duds, attempts, and puzzle outcome MUST be shared consistently across all connected players.

FR-021.title: Concurrent attempts to use the same pattern MUST produce no more than one effect.

FR-022.title: A reconnecting player MUST receive the current board and current pattern availability without regenerating the puzzle.

FR-023.title: Malformed, stale, tampered, repeated, or terminal-state pattern actions MUST leave puzzle state unchanged.

FR-024.title: Starting a fresh hacking attempt MUST discard the previous puzzle's pattern availability and used-pattern state.

context: area: existing hacking-game behavior and prior migrated specification
area: puzzle model, board generation, player protocol, player interface, and game-master control
constraint: remove every player cheat while preserving the trusted game-master solve control
constraint: exact bracket pairs and 80/20 special-pattern outcomes
intent: Restore Fallout-style hacking immersion by replacing player cheats with one-use special patterns while preserving a game-master solve override.
approach: Replace player administrator cheats with coordinate-addressed special patterns discovered and consumed in the server-owned Go hacking aggregate. Extend the existing live-service mutex and WebSocket/public projection path so effects are atomic, reconnect-safe, and presentation-only in the browser while preserving the Wails game-master solve override.

decisions.decision: Replace HACK_ADMIN and the SUCCESS entry with HACK_PATTERN while retaining ForceHackSuccess
decisions.why: Separates the untrusted player mechanic from the trusted game-master override
decisions.rejected: Reusing the administrator message or removing the GM override

decisions.decision: Identify patterns by column, opening index, and closing index and rediscover them from current board text
decisions.why: Coordinates distinguish stacked patterns and support dynamic discovery without exposing secrets
decisions.rejected: Text identities, client-trusted coordinates, or generation-only random IDs

decisions.decision: Construct and verify exactly 3-6 isolated initial patterns using bracket-free ordinary filler
decisions.why: Guarantees the required count at every difficulty without incidental bracket interactions
decisions.rejected: Retrying uncontrolled random boards or publishing only a subset

decisions.decision: Validate, consume, resolve, and project each pattern activation under the existing live-service mutex
decisions.why: Makes simultaneous use produce at most one effect and one complete shared snapshot

decisions.decision: Use Intn(100) buckets 0-79 for dud removal and 80-99 for attempt restoration
decisions.why: Implements the exact 80/20 split through the existing deterministic random seam
decisions.rejected: Floating-point probability or a no-op dud fallback

decisions.decision: Drive range highlighting and activation from the public patterns projection
decisions.why: Supports overlapping spans while keeping canonical availability on the server
decisions.rejected: Independent JavaScript discovery or overlapping DOM wrappers

decisions.decision: Extend HACK_STATE and TERMINAL_LIVE additively with patterns and reject removed HACK_ADMIN input
decisions.why: Reuses existing convergence and reconnect envelopes while ensuring stale clients cannot retain the cheat
decisions.rejected: A new protocol version or a separate pattern snapshot message

decisions.decision: Seed each generated special pattern as an isolated adjacent bracket pair
decisions.why: A two-cell span is valid under the contract and guarantees the exact count without cross-pair interactions while the scanner still supports longer dynamic and stacked spans
decisions.rejected: Variable-length generated spans that can accidentally create extra compatible pairs
